_why: 1.9.1-py.10 writes an owner's own title labels into an account's share filter: an ADMIT label as one
more alternative in every allow group, a HIDE label beside the row excludes. The movie half of 'an
OR'd label admits TITLES' was already recorded (pms_share_filter_allow_lists.json, 'grouping'). This
records the TV half, and what the code and the guide had only expected: a label on a SHOW carries the
show's episodes with it, in both directions.
Measured on the live server the day py.10 was deployed, by Shortlist's own privacy pass writing one
managed Home profile's filters (no hand-written filter), then reading AS that profile with its own
server token. All reads are GETs.
Conclusions the code and docs rely on:
1. A show rated OUTSIDE the allow list that carries the admit label is visible, and so is every one of
its episodes — on allLeaves and by key.
2. A show rated INSIDE the allow list that carries the hide label is a 404, and so is every episode.
3. Movies behave the same by key; unrated and 'Not Rated' titles are admitted by the label alone.
4. The admit label joined the existing own-row label clause ('label=Shortlist_kids,KidsAllow'); the
hide label joined the enforced exclude clause. The account's own rows stayed visible, nobody
